routes.description: Establish that finite, composite beings exhibit real essence, form, and received existence, requiring an external self-existent ground that accounts for their unity, diversity, and actuality and can be identified with the God of classical theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if objective essences and essence-existence composition are established, the required ground is shown to be necessary and external to contingent reality, and the inference reaches classical theism rather than an unspecified cause.

motionBridge.description: Show that the necessary self-existent ground inferred from contingent composition possesses the identity required by the God of classical theism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that form or essence is an objective feature of beings and is not exhausted by physical description, classification, language, or assigned use.
Establish a real distinction in finite beings between what they are and the act by which they exist, requiring an account of their conjunction.
Show that the unity of diverse parts and the composition of essence with existence require an external composing ground rather than an unexplained natural arrangement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Justify metaphysical reasoning about reality as a whole as an appropriate method for reaching conclusions unavailable from piecemeal empirical inquiry alone.
Specify how historical claims, reported miracles, prediction, explanatory scope, and personal experience could support identification of the necessary ground with a revealed God.

routes.description: Show that the proposed essence, composition, and necessary-ground claims lack independent demonstration and do not discriminate a divine agent from physical, descriptive, unknown, or non-agent explanations, leaving the classical-theist conclusion evidentially unwarranted.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the pro premises remain unsupported or adequately explained without additional metaphysical entities, the inference from grounding to agency or classical theism fails, and revelation or experience does not supply independently sufficient evidence.

motionBridge.description: Show that the presented considerations do not provide testable, independently supported, and discriminating evidence for the God of classical theism.

centralBridges.description: Require claims about God and metaphysical entities to receive support proportionate to their background plausibility and capable of distinguishing them from alternatives.
Account for identity, classification, form, and natural arrangement through physical properties, causal continuity, and human abstractions without positing independently existing essences.
Show that a need for explanation or causal grounding does not by itself establish intentional composition, a personal agent, or the God of classical theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Begin from observed beings and acknowledged uncertainty without classifying them as created or placing God among live explanations absent independent support.
Test claims of revelation and divine presence against sincere nonbelief, conflicting interpretation, and the apparent absence of clear universal disclosure.

sections.title: Metaphysical Method and Evidential Standards
sections.rationale: Determines whether reasoning about being as a whole can constitute good evidence and what independent support, testability, background knowledge, or explanatory discrimination the motion requires.

sections.title: Essence, Form, Identity, and Abstraction
sections.rationale: Addresses whether objective essences or forms exist beyond physical properties, causal continuity, classifications, linguistic concepts, intended functions, and changing material arrangements.

sections.title: Essence-Existence Composition and the Necessary Ground
sections.rationale: Covers the principal affirmative inference from finite beings whose essence and existence are distinct to a self-existent ground, together with objections to its premises and inferential validity.

sections.title: Composition, Causation, and the Inference to Agency
sections.rationale: Tests whether unity, diversity, parts, and observed effects require an external composer or personal cause, or whether that step assumes agency without discriminating evidence.

sections.title: From a Ground of Being to Classical Theism
sections.rationale: Examines whether the proposed necessary ground is adequately identified with the God of classical theism through philosophical identity claims, historical revelation, reported miracles, experience, and the challenge of divine hiddenness.
